E: Speed = distance ÷ time = 320 ÷ 4 = 80 km/h.

E: a = (v − u) ÷ t = (46 − 4) ÷ 7 = 6 m/s².

@topic phy-atomic

Q: A radioactive sample has a half-life of 2 days. What fraction of it remains after 6 days?
A: 1/8
W: 1/6
W: 1/3
W: 1/16
E: 6 days is 3 half-lives, so (½)³ = 1/8 remains.

Q: A radioactive sample has a half-life of 10 hours. What fraction of it remains after 30 hours?
A: 1/8
W: 1/6
W: 1/3
W: 1/16
E: 30 hours is 3 half-lives, so (½)³ = 1/8 remains.

Q: A radioactive sample has a half-life of 10 hours. What fraction of it remains after 50 hours?
A: 1/32
W: 1/10
W: 1/5
W: 1/64
E: 50 hours is 5 half-lives, so (½)⁵ = 1/32 remains.

Q: A radioactive sample has a half-life of 2 days. What fraction of it remains after 8 days?
A: 1/16
W: 1/8
W: 1/4
W: 1/32
E: 8 days is 4 half-lives, so (½)⁴ = 1/16 remains.

Q: A radioactive sample has a half-life of 5 minutes. What fraction of it remains after 25 minutes?
A: 1/32
W: 1/10
W: 1/5
W: 1/64
E: 25 minutes is 5 half-lives, so (½)⁵ = 1/32 remains.

Q: A radioactive sample has a half-life of 30 minutes. What fraction of it remains after 120 minutes?
A: 1/16
W: 1/8
W: 1/4
W: 1/32
E: 120 minutes is 4 half-lives, so (½)⁴ = 1/16 remains.

@topic phy-gas-laws

Q: A gas occupies 2 L at 300 kPa. What volume does it occupy at 100 kPa if the temperature is constant?
A: 6 L
W: 0.67 L
W: 2 L
W: 0 L
E: Boyle's law: P₁V₁ = P₂V₂, so V₂ = 300 × 2 ÷ 100 = 6 L.

Q: A gas occupies 12 L at 150 kPa. What volume does it occupy at 200 kPa if the temperature is constant?
A: 9 L
W: 16 L
W: 12 L
W: 12.5 L
E: Boyle's law: P₁V₁ = P₂V₂, so V₂ = 150 × 12 ÷ 200 = 9 L.

Q: A gas occupies 6 L at 150 kPa. What volume does it occupy at 50 kPa if the temperature is constant?
A: 18 L
W: 2 L
W: 6 L
W: 5 L
E: Boyle's law: P₁V₁ = P₂V₂, so V₂ = 150 × 6 ÷ 50 = 18 L.

A: 16 L
W: 4 L
W: 8 L
W: 7 L
E: Boyle's law: P₁V₁ = P₂V₂, so V₂ = 200 × 8 ÷ 100 = 16 L.

@topic phy-machines

Q: A machine with a velocity ratio of 4 lifts a load of 150 N with an effort of 50 N. Find its efficiency.
A: 75%
W: 133.3%
W: 3%
W: 37.5%
E: MA = 150 ÷ 50 = 3. Efficiency = MA ÷ VR × 100% = 3/4 × 100% = 75%.

Q: A machine with a velocity ratio of 5 lifts a load of 400 N with an effort of 100 N. Find its efficiency.
A: 80%
W: 125%
W: 4%
W: 40%
E: MA = 400 ÷ 100 = 4. Efficiency = MA ÷ VR × 100% = 4/5 × 100% = 80%.

Q: A machine with a velocity ratio of 5 lifts a load of 300 N with an effort of 150 N. Find its efficiency.
A: 40%
W: 250%
W: 2%
W: 20%
E: MA = 300 ÷ 150 = 2. Efficiency = MA ÷ VR × 100% = 2/5 × 100% = 40%.

A: 66.7%
W: 150%
W: 4%
W: 33.4%
E: MA = 480 ÷ 120 = 4. Efficiency = MA ÷ VR × 100% = 4/6 × 100% = 66.7%.
